title: Intelligence per watt: measuring intelligence efficiency of local AI
org: Saad-Falcon, Hennessy, Mirhoseini, Ré et al.
gist: Measures task accuracy per unit of power for more than 20 local models on 8 accelerators over a million real single-turn queries, and argues a large and rising share of everyday queries can be answered locally, which favours hybrid routing.
changes: The quantitative case for local: most queries do not need the frontier. Its own data also show local accelerators doing less per watt than cloud ones on the same model.
caveats: Single-turn chat and reasoning only. It says nothing about agent workloads with long contexts, which are what the rest of this site is about.

numbers.metric: Share of queries local models answer correctly

numbers.baseline: the same measure two years earlier

numbers.metric: Efficiency of local accelerators on identical models

bears_on.note: Local is good enough for most single-turn queries and less efficient per watt. Agent workloads are untested.
